Determination of Value of Supply as per CGST Rules, 2017 for S Anand Lakshmi Forex Solutions Private Limited

(1) Value of Supply under Rule 32(2)(b) of the CGST Rules, 2017
Rule 32(2)(b) provides that value in relation to the supply of foreign currency, including money changing shall be deemed to be

| S. No. | Currency exchanged | Value of supply |
|---|---|---|
| 1. | Upto ₹ 1,00,000 | 1% of the gross amount of currency exchanged OR ₹ 250 whichever is higher |
| 2. | Exceeding ₹ 1,00,000 and upto ₹ 10,00,000 | ₹ 1,000 + 0.50% of the (gross amount of currency exchanged - ₹ 1,00,000) |
| 3. | Exceeding ₹ 10,00,000 | ₹ 5,500 + 0.1% of the (gross amount of currency exchanged - ₹ 10,00,000) OR ₹ 60,000 whichever is lower |

Case 1: For the purchase of 1,200 USD from Bincon traders:
Gross amount of currency exchanged: $\text{₹ }79 \times 1{,}200 = 94{,}800$
Since the amount is less than ₹ 1,00,000, the value of supply is 1% of the gross amount or ₹ 250, whichever is higher. i.e. 948 or 250
Therefore, Value of supply $= \text{₹ }948$

Case 2: For the sale of 2,600 USD to Meera Exports:
Gross amount of currency exchanged: $\text{₹ }78 \times 2{,}600 = \text{₹ }2{,}02{,}800$
Since the amount exceeds ₹ 1,00,000 but is less than ₹ 10,00,000, the value of supply is $\text{₹ }1{,}000 + 0.50\%\text{ of }(\text{₹ }2{,}02{,}800 - \text{₹ }1{,}00{,}000)$.
$1000+ 514$
Therefore, Value of supply $= \text{₹ }1{,}514$

(2) Value of Supply under Rule 32(2)(a) of the CGST Rules, 2017
Key Aspects of Rule 32(2)(a) and related provisions:
• Rule 32(2)(a) of the CGST Rules, 2017, It enables the supplier to calculate the value based on the difference between the RBI rate and buying/selling rate, If RBI Reference Rate is available
• If no RBI Reference Rate: the rate determined by 1% of the gross amount of Indian Rupees provided or received.
• No Indian Rupees Involved: If neither currency exchanged is Indian Rupees, the value is 1% of the lesser of the two amounts that the person changing the money would have received by converting into Indian Rupees at the RBI reference rate, say

Case 1: For the purchase of 1,200 USD from Bincon traders:
$(\text{RBI reference rate} - \text{transaction rate}) \times \text{Amount in USD}$
Calculation: $(\text{₹ }80.80 - \text{₹ }79) \times 1{,}200\text{ USD}$
Therefore, Value of supply $= \text{₹ }2{,}160$

Case 2: For the sale of 2,600 USD to Meera Exports:
$1\%\text{ of }(\text{Transaction rate} \times \text{Amount in USD})$
Calculation: $1\%\text{ of }(\text{₹ }78 \times 2{,}600\text{ USD})$
Value of supply $= \text{₹ }2{,}028$
